NMADTA implements two established Bayesian model families for networks of
diagnostic tests. Both combine studies with different observed test sets,
including studies with and without a reference standard.

## Hierarchical model

[`nmadt.hierarchical()`](../reference/nmadt.hierarchical.html) directly models
accuracy parameters, including sensitivity and specificity, with between-study
random effects. Pooled sensitivity and specificity are natural summary quantities.
The model is described by Ma, Lian, Chu, Ibrahim, and Chen (2018),
[Biostatistics](https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxx025).

~~~r
library(NMADTA)
data(dat.kang)

fit <- nmadt.hierarchical(
  nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography")
)
~~~

## HSROC model

[`nmadt.hsroc()`](../reference/nmadt.hsroc.html) uses accuracy and threshold
components. This parameterization is useful for considering differences
in operating thresholds across studies and comparisons across the ROC space.
The model is described by Lian, Hodges, and Chu (2019),
[Journal of the American Statistical Association](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2018.1476239).

~~~r
fit_hsroc <- nmadt.hsroc(
  nstu = 12, K = 2, data = dat.kang,
  testname = c("D-dimer", "Ultrasonography"),
  n.adapt = 5000, n.iter = 50000, n.chains = 3
)
~~~

## A common result interface

Both families return an object of class `nmadt`:

~~~r
print(fit)
summary(fit)
plot(fit, type = "sroc")
plot(fit, type = "forest")
plot(fit, type = "density")
plot(fit, type = "contour")
~~~

Summaries include posterior estimates and intervals for sensitivity,
specificity, prevalence, predictive values, and likelihood ratios.
Each model has its own prior parameters; consult the reference before
changing defaults.

## Missing data and priors

Changing between hierarchical and HSROC formulations does not resolve
uncertainty about why tests are missing. Regular functions use the MAR
formulation; [MNAR functions](missing-data.html) support sensitivity analysis.

Priors are specified on different scales in the two model families.
Similar-looking default settings need not express equivalent prior
information. For sparse networks or few reference-standard studies, examine
identification, convergence, and prior sensitivity.
The [software article](https://doi.org/10.1017/rsm.2026.10097) discusses
these choices and the implementation's limits.
